svg.title: Identifiability of the heater and probe lags
svg.desc: Early in the step, a heater with gain 0.2 and time constant 5 seconds and one with gain 0.4 and 10 seconds differ by only 0.018 degrees; after 10 seconds they differ by 0.8 degrees and the water follows the first. The two-store fit of the noisy probe gives lags of 5.1 and 1.8 seconds that fit equally well in either order. The water reference reaches 63.2 percent of its change 6 seconds after the step, so the water's lag is 5 seconds and the shorter lag belongs to the probe.
svg.text: What the step record can tell apart
Control Studio recording · step 75 → 85 % at 5.0 s · probe measured with a bounded ±0.05 °C error · numbers answer the predictions
Two-store fit: lags 5.1 s and 1.8 s, either order
1 s after the delay: 0.018 °C apart, too close
10 s after: 0.799 °C apart; the water follows K 0.2, τ 5 s
Fitted lags 5.1 s and 1.8 s, delay 1.1 s: the error shifts them from 5 s and 2 s
Either order gives this curve: the fit cannot say which lag is the probe's
63.2 % at 6.0 s after the step: the water's lag is 5 s, so 1.8 s is the probe's
